title: XAYOL TUSHUNCHASI VA UNING PSIXOLOGIK ASOSLARI
journal: New Uzbekistan Journal of Academic Research
abstract: Mazkur tezisda kognitiv jarayonlarning muhim tarkibiy qismi bo‘lgan xayol tushunchasi va uning psixologik asoslari, yangi obrazlarni shakllantirish mexanizmlari hamda shaxs kamolotidagi amaliy-pedagogik ahamiyati ilmiy va amaliy jihatdan keng yoritilgan. Tadqiqot jarayonida xayol jarayonining psixologik va neyropsixologik qonuniyatlarini to‘g‘ri rejalashtirish hamda ta’lim-tarbiya jarayoniga joriy etish insonlarning bilish jarayonlarini (tafakkur, xotira, diqqat), ijodiy salohiyatini va emotsional-irodaviy barqarorligini oshirish mexanizmlari tahlil qilingan. Maqolada umumiy va kognitiv psixologiya tamoyillari asosida faoliyatni tashkil etishning samaradorligi hamda shaxsni har tomonlama barkamol etib shakllantirishdagi o‘rni ochib berilgan.

title: When brand extension strategy meets sensory execution: the interactive effects of brand fit and sensory modality on perceived sub-brand value
journal: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
abstract: Purpose Drawing on brand ecosystem theory and expectation confirmation theory, this study examines how the interaction between parent-subsidiary brand fit types (high fit, low fit, Janus fit) and sensory modalities (proximal vs distal) influences perceived sub-brand value. It further investigates the mediating role of region-of-origin image and the moderating role of agricultural product category. Design/methodology/approach This study employs two scenario-based experiments (total N = 590 after exclusions). Study 1 manipulates fit type and sensory modality through offline physical exposure combined with sensory transfer guidance; Study 2 replicates and extends the design using online consumer review scenarios with text-based sensory priming, while additionally manipulating agricultural product category (primary vs processed). Findings The results reveal a significant interactive effect between parent-sub-brand fit types and sensory modality on perceived sub-brand value. Specifically, distal (sight/sound) cues outperform proximal (taste/touch) cues under high-fit conditions, whereas the reverse holds under low-fit conditions; Janus-fit extensions generate higher perceived sub-brand value than high-fit and low-fit extensions when averaged across sensory modalities. The mediating role of region-of-origin image is conditional, being significant only under proximal sensory processing but not under distal processing. Furthermore, agricultural product category shapes the strength and pattern of the fit-sensory interaction, with a more systematic pattern observed for processed products, whereas for primary products, the sensory advantage emerges only under low-fit conditions. Originality/value This research integrates Janus fit into agricultural geographical brand extension, develops a strategic-tactical coordination perspective linking strategic and tactical levels and expands the combined application scope of brand ecosystem and expectation confirmation theories.

title: What factors predict the innovation of Chinese family firms: empirical evidence based on machine learning
abstract: Purpose Prior studies on family firm innovation have focused primarily on causal explanations and isolated variable significance, but lack a prediction-oriented approach that systematically compares the relative importance of multiple predictors. Drawing on the capability–willingness–pressure framework, this paper aims to identify the key predictors of innovation in Chinese family firms and to reconcile inconsistent findings in prior research. By integrating a prediction-oriented perspective to complement traditional causal inference, this study examines how the family, firm and environmental characteristics jointly predict innovation input and output. Design/methodology/approach Based on a systematic review of 102 empirical studies, this paper constructs a multidimensional framework encompassing 30 predictors across family, firm and external environmental factors. Using Chinese A-share listed family firms from 2010 to 2024, the final samples include 10,078 firm-year observations for R&D investment and 10,145 firm-year observations for R&D output. R&D investment is measured by R&D intensity, while R&D output is measured by patent applications. The study uses the gradient boosting regression tree algorithm. Relative importance measures and partial dependence plots are used to evaluate predictive power and uncover nonlinear boundaries. Rolling-window out-of-sample tests are conducted to assess model performance. Findings The results show that the gradient boosting regression trees (GBRT) model outperforms traditional linear benchmark models in predicting both R&D investment and output. In the integrated model, GBRT achieves rolling-window out-of-sample R-squared values of 30.656% for R&D investment and 43.086% for R&D output, compared with 13.266% and 31.294% for ordinary least squares, respectively. Family ownership involvement, digital transformation, clan culture, ownership balance and industry competition emerge as the core predictors. Crucially, these features exhibit distinct nonlinear tipping points. By identifying the specific ranges where moderate levels are positively associated with innovation and excessive levels may weaken or reverse these associations, the predictive model identifies nonlinear boundary patterns that are consistent with different theoretical expectations in prior research. These nonlinear boundary patterns provide a potential explanation for previously conflicting empirical findings. Practical implications The findings offer actionable implications for multiple stakeholders. For family business managers, the results provide a specific blueprint for balancing family control with appropriate ownership checks and strengthening digital transformation to support innovation investment and patent output. In particular, moderate ownership balance may help support innovation output, whereas excessive family ownership concentration may weaken innovation incentives. For policymakers, the study highlights the necessity of tailoring regional innovation support and technological subsidies to account for localized clan cultures and varying degrees of industry competition. In regions with strong clan culture or intense industry competition, policy support may need to place greater emphasis on governance professionalization, external knowledge access and mechanisms that reduce the risk of innovation investment. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by introducing a prediction-oriented capability–willingness–pressure framework to family firm innovation research. It moves beyond isolated variable significance to identify the relative predictive importance, nonlinear patterns and boundary conditions of key predictors, thereby helping reconcile previously conflicting empirical findings.

title: Warranty and service contracts for reliable service quality: a traceability-based framework
journal: International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management
abstract: Purpose This paper develops a conceptual framework for examining how warranty and long-term service agreements may shape maintenance decisions, service quality and auditability in asset-intensive settings. Design/methodology/approach The paper synthesizes literature on warranty management, service contracts, reliability, maintenance documentation and servitization. It presents a Reliability Decision Architecture (RDA), conceptual decision equations, five propositions and three illustrative contractual archetypes. Findings The synthesis identifies four proposed distortion mechanisms: metric narrowing, asymmetric risk transfer, evidentiary under-specification and oversight decoupling. The RDA links contract clauses to feasible maintenance choices and their reviewability. Effects on reliability, availability and lifecycle cost remain propositions requiring validation. Research limitations/implications The framework is conceptual. The archetypes vary several clauses together and provide neither causal identification nor empirical validation. A qualitative evidence checklist supports review; numerical scoring and the proposed decision relationships require testing. Practical implications Managers can use the framework to examine whether metrics, evidence duties, escalation rules and review rights support feasible, reviewable maintenance choices. Documentation burdens and excessive risk transfer also require consideration. Originality/value The contribution is an integrative diagnostic architecture distinguishing technical admissibility, contractual feasibility and private attractiveness, with evidence and review requirements made explicit at each maintenance decision.

title: Trypanosomes Maintain Propulsion in Confined Environments by Modulating Rotational Motility from Swimming to Network-Threading Propulsion
abstract: Abstract The parasite Trypanosoma brucei lives in the body fluids of its hosts, including blood and interstitial fluids of various tissues. The mechanism of dissemination within these environments remains largely unresolved, although the trypanosome´s motility is known to play an essential role for its survival. The unicellular flagellate is a versatile microswimmer, like bacteria or sperm cells, albeit structurally more complex than these classical models. Here we study their motility in different viscous and elastic regimes. Using quantitative high speed video microscopy and digital holography microscopy, we detail the three-dimensional mechanical reaction of the flexible cell body with its uniquely attached flagellum to increasing confinement, leading to a network-threading type propulsion. This allows stable progressive motility despite a reduction in wave parameters up to tissue-like confinement. We thus show how trypanosomes can mechanically adjust in response to various microenvironments and, using flagellar beat reversal, manage the exploration of their complex environments.

title: Transformational leadership, psychological safety, and work engagement in family businesses: the indirect roles of resilience and job satisfaction
abstract: Purpose This study examines how transformational leadership is associated with work engagement in family businesses through interconnected relational, personal and attitudinal pathways involving psychological safety, resilience and job satisfaction, while also assessing the complete sequential indirect association among these constructs. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 800 employees working in Portuguese family businesses and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement and structural models, direct and indirect associations, predictive performance and potential endogeneity were assessed. Findings Transformational leadership was positively associated with psychological safety and work engagement. Psychological safety was positively associated with resilience, job satisfaction and work engagement, while resilience was positively associated with job satisfaction and work engagement. Job satisfaction was also positively associated with work engagement. Furthermore, several statistically significant indirect associations linked transformational leadership with work engagement through psychological safety, resilience and job satisfaction. The complete sequential indirect association was statistically significant but very small in magnitude (ß = 0.005), indicating that the findings are better characterised by multiple interconnected pathways, with the complete sequential indirect association representing only one component of this broader pattern. Practical implications Family businesses may support employee engagement by attending to transformational leadership, psychological safety, resilience and employees' evaluations of their jobs. These implications should not be interpreted as evidence of causal intervention effects. Originality/value The study extends family-business research beyond the established transformational leadership–psychological safety–engagement relationship by integrating relational, personal and attitudinal components within a broader pattern of direct and indirect associations. In doing so, it applies Conservation of Resources theory to provide a more differentiated explanation of employee engagement in family businesses.

title: The Establishment, Development, and Educational Role of MI Al-Amin Sinongko
journal: Journal of Economics, Law, and Humanities
abstract: Background/Introduction: The history of MI Al-Amin Sinongko illustrates how local initiatives can support the provision of Islamic primary education. Research Objectives: This study traces the madrasah’s establishment, examines its institutional development, and describes its educational role in Sinongko. Methodology: The study used a qualitative historical approach. The study examined interviews and madrasah documents through source collection, source criticism, interpretation, and historiography. Results: The madrasah was established in 2007 through cooperation between the Al-Mukmin Foundation and local community members, using waqf land. It expanded from one building to four and offered regular Qur’an memorization (tahfiz) programs. Two alumni recalled experiences related to worship, memorization, and discipline. One alumnus also felt that religious instruction left less time for general subjects. Unique Contribution: The study connects the community’s role in establishing the madrasah with its subsequent development and alumni experiences. Conclusion: The madrasah provided local families with an option for Islamic primary education. Its wider influence on the community remains uncertain. Recommendations: Future research should use comparable school records and include parents and residents to examine changes in educational access.

title: Serum proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 levels correlate with depression severity in post-stroke patients
abstract: BACKGROUND Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a common neuropsychiatric complication affecting an estimated 30%-40% of stroke survivors and adversely affecting rehabilitation and quality of life. Emerging evidence suggests that proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) may be involved in neuroinflammation and mood regulation. Evolocumab, a PCSK9 inhibitor, may have effects beyond lipid lowering when added to statin therapy; however, its association with depressive symptoms in patients with PSD remains unclear. AIM To investigate the association between serum PCSK9 levels and depression severity in patients with PSD receiving evolocumab plus statin therapy and to assess the association of this combination with changes in depressive symptoms. METHODS This retrospective study included 128 patients with PSD: 64 received evolocumab (140 mg every 2 weeks) plus atorvastatin (20 mg daily), and 64 received atorvastatin alone (20 mg daily). The primary outcomes were serum PCSK9 concentrations and 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17) scores at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, and 12. Secondary outcomes included Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAMA) scores, lipid profiles, inflammatory markers [interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein], and cognitive function assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Correlation analyses examined associations between PCSK9 concentrations and clinical outcomes. RESULTS At week 12, serum PCSK9 levels decreased from 385.6 ± 78.4 ng/mL to 156.3 ± 42.1 ng/mL in the combination-therapy group, compared with 378.2 ± 76.9 ng/mL to 298.5 ± 68.7 ng/mL in the atorvastatin-only group (P < 0.001). HAMD-17 scores decreased from 22.8 ± 4.5 to 10.2 ± 3.1 and from 22.3 ± 4.2 to 14.6 ± 3.8, respectively (P < 0.001 for the between-group comparison at week 12). Serum PCSK9 levels were positively correlated with HAMD-17 scores at week 12 (r = 0.652, P < 0.001). Compared with the atorvastatin-only group, the combination-therapy group had lower week-12 HAMA scores (8.5 ± 2.3 vs 12.1 ± 3.2, P < 0.001) and IL-6 concentrations (3.2 ± 0.8 pg/mL vs 5.1 ± 1.2 pg/mL, P < 0.001), higher MoCA scores (25.8 ± 2.1 vs 23.4 ± 2.6, P = 0.001), and a higher depression treatment response rate (73.4% vs 48.4%, P = 0.003). CONCLUSION In this retrospective, evolocumab added to atorvastatin was associated with greater reductions in serum PCSK9 levels and depressive symptom scores than atorvastatin alone. The correlation between PCSK9 concentrations and depression severity suggests that PCSK9 warrants further investigation as a potential biomarker in PSD. Prospective studies are needed to establish whether PCSK9 inhibition improves depressive symptoms.
